title: fugaro/project-layer.yaml
description: A Fugaro project's layer: project-wide defaults and workflow profiles for every repository whose fugaro.yaml names the project and its gcp_project. See docs/project-layer.md.

auth.description: Where the run's model calls are authenticated. cascade asks for the project's credentials cascade (docs/credentials-service): it is refused with followup.allow_public, needs budget.mode observe or enforce, and is enabled only by the project policy's routing.claude: {via: cascade}, which only the operator can set. Fugaro before 0.10.0 refuses the value.

levels.description: Each review level's own settings for every repository of this project (L1.3, D722; config.ReviewLevels), merged into a repository's own agent.levels one key at a time: a repository that pins level 2 keeps this block's level 1. `none: true` here is how the project turns a level off everywhere; a repository may not turn it back on against the owner's floor (L1.4). Fugaro before 0.16.0 refuses the key, in every repository of the project.

adversarial_rounds.description: Review level 3's round count for every repository of the project (L1.3, D726): 1 to 10, and absent leaves the resolved rigor mode's own senior row (rigor.AdversarialDefault). A repository's own agent.adversarial_rounds replaces it. Needs fugaro 0.16.0.

rigor.description: The rigor mode every repository of this project runs at, and the area rules in effect for all of them (docs/rigor-modes/spec.md D20). Both keys may also be set in a repository's own rigor: block, and the two areas lists are a union, not a replacement: a repository's own rules never switch the project's off. Fugaro before 0.11.0 refuses the key, in every repository of the project.

default.description: The mode a run of any repository of this project resolves to when the repository sets none. Needs fugaro 0.11.0.

areas.description: The project's named path rules, in effect beside each repository's own. Needs fugaro 0.11.0.

claude_models.description: Explicit Claude model IDs a route the installation config defines also serves (design/mixed-credentials.md §4, docs/project-layer.md §6): provider name -> one explicit "anthropic/<id>" per entry, never a pattern and never a class. A name the installation config does not define, an empty list, or an entry overlapping another route's pattern is refused by `fugaro validate` and `fugaro config publish`, the surfaces that hold the installation's whole route table. A run does not refuse it: a claim naming a route the job's own table does not carry (a repository the provider's allow_data_to does not list has no such route in its job) is dropped, so the claim enables nothing and a pin on that ID is refused as a model no provider serves, before any call. Each entry is a route's own model entry once merged, so it is judged by the route-entry rule too: at most 100 characters (config.CheckModelPattern), the same bound the gateway's routes apply.

ab.description: The project's model A/B sampling (docs/model-ab-testing, D550-D573): whether its first code runs are sampled, which other models may run as the challenger, which model judges a pair, and how much extra median cost per pair a mode accepts before keeping the champion. A top-level key of the layer file, like governance and unlike defaults: a repository's own ab: block may only set rate: 0, its opt-out, so the two meet only in the merge, which takes the lower rate and nothing else of this block from the repository (D556). Nothing reads these keys to launch a pair before fugaro 0.15.0: the block is inert until then. A null block, or a key written as null or 0, sets nothing.

rate.description: The share of eligible runs sampled, sampled by a hash of the run ID below the rate. 0 (the default) is off, and 0.10 is the ceiling (D557).

max_pairs_per_day.description: The most pairs one repository is sampled for per UTC day, counted by the launcher from today's challenger records. 0 or null takes Fugaro's 5 (D557).

challengers.description: The models the owner allows as a challenger, in priority order (D556). A repository may never name one: a repository author could otherwise send that repository's code to a provider the owner opened only to others. Each entry must be a model ID (or a prefix ending in *, the spelling a route entry uses); every model named is checked again at launch against the repository's job, its allow-list and the price table. The pattern here is the shape of an entry only: the decoder's CheckModelPattern also refuses a claim on Claude models and a prefix too broad to name, and a repository's CI checking this file has no such rule.

judge_model.description: The model a pair's blind judge run uses (D553). The owner's alone, like challengers.

exchange_rate.description: The extra median cost a pair may carry, as a fraction of the champion's median cost, before the mode keeps the champion (D565). A mode left out takes the figure Fugaro ships: 0 for POC, 0.25 for Startup, 0.5 for Pro, 2 for Critical (and hotfix, which is never sampled, 0).

governance.description: The guardrails every repository of this project runs under (docs/task-governance/spec.md §2, §5). A top-level key of the layer file, like claude_models and unlike defaults: the block is a policy the project sets for all its repositories, and a repository's own governance: block can only tighten it (docs/project-layer.md §5). This is the one layer that may loosen Fugaro's defaults, up to the per-run cap, which stays the ceiling: a stage budget is a fraction under it (G6). A null block, or a key written as null or 0, sets nothing and takes the default.

review_ratio.description: N, the ratio guardrail: review calls above N times the implement stage's calls stop the stage. Fugaro's default is 5.

review_floor_calls.description: The review-call count below which the ratio is not applied at all, so a short implementation is still reviewed. Fugaro's default is 20.

max_subagents.description: The most distinct sub-agents one stage may start, concurrently or in total. Fugaro's default is 5.

stage_budget.description: A stage's share of the run's budget. Implement and review are fractions of the per-run cap, review counting the first-line and the senior review together; fix is a fraction of the implement stage's own budget. Fugaro's defaults are 0.7, 0.5 and 0.5.

implement.description: The implement stage's share of the per-run cap.

review.description: The review stage's share of the per-run cap, first-line and senior review together.

fix.description: The fix stage's share of the implement stage's own budget, not of the per-run cap.

stage_tokens.description: A stage's token ceiling, in tokens. Unset by default: a stage with no ceiling of its own is bounded by the run's own agent.max_run_tokens.

implement.description: The implement stage's token ceiling; unset by default.

review.description: The review stage's token ceiling; unset by default.

fix.description: The fix stage's token ceiling; unset by default.

stage_timeout.description: A stage's own wall-clock ceiling; unset by default. The run's workflows.*.timeouts.stage still bounds it.

implement.description: The implement stage's own wall-clock ceiling; unset by default.

review.description: The review stage's own wall-clock ceiling; unset by default.

fix.description: The fix stage's own wall-clock ceiling; unset by default.

tiers.description: What a run of each expectation tier is expected to cost and take, and how far one of its stages may fan out (docs/task-governance/spec.md §3, G6). The project sets the expectation its repositories run under, and a repository's own block can only tighten it. A tier is an expectation and never a cap: the deployed per-run cap stays the ceiling, so an expected_usd above it is an expectation the run still stops at the cap for, and no key here moves a cap. A key written as null or 0 sets nothing and takes the tier's default. Fugaro ships trivial $0.25/10m, small $1/30m, medium $3/90m and large $8/240m, with max_subagents 3 for trivial and small and 5 for medium and large.

trivial.description: The trivial tier's expectation: a copy or text tweak of a few lines. Fugaro's default is $0.25, 10 minutes, 3 sub-agents.

small.description: The small tier's expectation: a single-file feature or bug fix. Fugaro's default is $1, 30 minutes, 3 sub-agents.

medium.description: The medium tier's expectation: a multi-file change with tests. Fugaro's default is $3, 90 minutes, 5 sub-agents.

large.description: The large tier's expectation: a cross-cutting refactor. Fugaro's default is $8, 240 minutes, 5 sub-agents.

level.description: One review level's settings (config.LevelSetting). The keys are the Go field names except `none`, which is config.LevelSetting.Off: `none` is what an owner or a launcher writes to say a level does not run, where `off: true` would read as a value rather than as a level's absence. Three of the decoder's rules are not expressible here, and are refused by config.ReviewLevels.Validate instead: an effort outside `effort`'s five values (config.Efforts; Claude Code itself warns and sends the model's default for the flag, and drops the environment variable and the settings key in silence, so nothing downstream refuses one), a focus carrying a control character, a bidi or zero-width one, a line or paragraph separator, or invalid UTF-8 (the project layer's own rule for a value out of a file, internal/config's badRune, which is why the pattern here cannot carry it), and `none: true` beside any other key, which is refused rather than read — a level that is off has no settings. The bound is a byte count while maxLength counts characters, so this schema is the looser of the two for text outside ASCII: a focus of 500 ASCII characters is at both caps, and one of 500 characters outside ASCII is over the decoder's and under this one's.

model.description: The exact model ID this level runs (config.LevelSetting.Model). Absent leaves the level on the model its own layer resolves — agent.models.reviewer for a senior level — and it is bounded by allowed_models as every other model setting is, which the runner checks rather than this schema.

effort.description: The reasoning effort this level runs at (config.LevelSetting.Effort, config.Efforts): the five values the pinned Claude Code accepts, from the least to the most, as measured against Claude Code 2.1.283 (docs/multi-model.md). Absent asks for none, which is the model's own default — that is not the same as "auto" or "unset", which are not values here. The vocabulary is closed in both directions: a value outside it is refused by config.ReviewLevels.Validate, because Claude Code would take it without a word.

none.description: True turns this level off (config.LevelSetting.Off): the level's step is not run, and the three settings beside it are refused rather than read. False, and an absent key, both mean the level runs. A level that is off under the owner's floor is refused at launch (L3.1, L1.4), which is not this schema's rule: nothing here reads the floor.

focus.description: What this level's reviewer is asked to look at, in the launcher's own words (config.LevelSetting.Focus). It is data and never a command: the runner puts it in the reviewer's prompt as quoted text, and it is never put through a shell or joined into a path. 500 is config.MaxLevelFocusBytes, which the decoder applies as a byte count as well.

stageFraction.description: A stage's share of a budget, as a fraction. 0 or null sets nothing and takes Fugaro's default, and 1 or more is refused: the per-run cap stays the ceiling whatever a stage is given (G6).

stageTokens.description: A stage's token ceiling, in tokens; 0 or null sets nothing.

tierLimits.description: One expectation tier's figures (docs/task-governance/spec.md §3, G6). Every key is an expectation and never a cap: the deployed per-run cap stays the ceiling whatever is written here. 0 or null sets nothing and takes the tier's default. The same shape as fugaro.schema.json's.

expected_usd.description: What a run of this tier is expected to cost, in dollars. 0 or null sets nothing. An expectation above the deployed per-run cap is still only an expectation: the run stops at the cap (G6).

expected_minutes.description: What a run of this tier is expected to take, in minutes. 0 or null sets nothing.

max_subagents.description: How far one stage of a run of this tier may fan out, at most the same 100 governance.max_subagents is bounded by. 0 or null sets nothing.

rigorMode.description: A rigor mode, spelled exactly as fugaro's own vocabulary spells it (internal/rigor). See fugaro.schema.json's rigorMode; the two layers' blocks carry the same keys and the same values.

rigorArea.description: One rigor.areas rule: a name to print, a doublestar path glob relative to the repository root, and the mode it sets. The same shape as fugaro.schema.json's.

name.description: The rule's name, which the run record, the pull request body and fugaro watch print when they say which rule decided. 1 to 40 characters of letters, digits, space, dash, underscore and dot, starting with a letter or a digit.

match.description: A doublestar path glob relative to the repository root. Not empty, not absolute, no ".." component, and a pattern doublestar validates.

mode.description: The mode this rule sets for the paths it matches.

base.$comment: not: {} forbids this key outright (matches nothing), including an explicit null: the removed-key tombstone idiom (6x across fugaro.schema.json and project-layer.schema.json: base, image.node and image.jdk), not dead code. It keeps the key documented in an editor's tooltip (see description) while still refusing any value. Do not delete when touching this key.
base.description: Removed in 0.7.0: delete it and declare runtimes in mise.toml (docs/base-image-migration.md)

checkout.description: The same three values as fugaro.schema.json's workflows.*.checkout: baked (default), clone, and shared, which runs a shared dependency-layer image and clones the source at launch, so a profile under it may carry image.apt, image.tools and image.skip_build_scripts but not image.setup.

node.$comment: not: {} forbids this key outright (matches nothing), including an explicit null: the removed-key tombstone idiom (6x across fugaro.schema.json and project-layer.schema.json: base, image.node and image.jdk), not dead code. It keeps the key documented in an editor's tooltip (see description) while still refusing any value. Do not delete when touching this key.
node.description: Removed in 0.7.0: declare node in mise.toml ([tools] node = "24") or in image.tools (docs/base-image-migration.md)

jdk.$comment: not: {} forbids this key outright (matches nothing), including an explicit null: the removed-key tombstone idiom (6x across fugaro.schema.json and project-layer.schema.json: base, image.node and image.jdk), not dead code. It keeps the key documented in an editor's tooltip (see description) while still refusing any value. Do not delete when touching this key.
jdk.description: Removed in 0.7.0: declare Java in mise.toml ([tools] java = "temurin-25") (docs/base-image-migration.md)
